text:
harper (support): FYI BetaApps just escalated - p99 on /v1/chat up from ~200ms to 3.2s in the last 90m. Customer noticed immediately after last night's maintenance window.

diego (sre): region? model? any error spikes or just latency?

harper (support): eu-central-1, model=embedder-lite (hosted), no 5xxs, a few client-side retries, but elevated latency and occasional "connection reset" from downstream LB reported.

li (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a cohort of hosts with high GPU stall counters and blocked NVMe IO. Kernel soft hang traces on a couple of nodes. Starting to look like storage + firmware interaction.

sam (infra): We pushed a GPU firmware microcode (v11.2.3) and a driver bump (540.11) during the maintenance window at 01:50 UTC. Also ran snapshot consolidation jobs for model shards at 02:05.

diego (sre): timeline lines up. Can we get a quick iostat and nvidia-smi from one affected host (gpu-node-17)?

maintenance-bot: retrieving logs for gpu-node-17 (xfer id: log-9921)

li (eng-runtime): logs pasted:
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s  wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         4.00   210.00   2560  163840  45.2   3.8   100.0
```
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv,noheader
98 %, 93 %, 78 C
```
```
$ dmesg | tail -n 40
[23456.123456] nvme nvme0: I/O 987654 timeout, aborting command
[23456.123460] nvidia: GPU lockup - stopping kernel thread
[23456.123470] pci 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received: Multiple Uncorr Err
```

diego (sre): NVMe saturated + GPU kernel hangs + PCIe errors. Not good. Even if GPU fully utilized, we shouldn't see NVMe blocking causing kernel hangs.

sam (infra): I've seen vendor notes recently about firmware v11.2.x interacting poorly with certain NVMe firmware revisions under heavy write consolidation. We'll pause snapshot consolidation and start rollback of GPU firmware on a small canary.

li (eng-runtime): Runtime mitigation: routing policy updated to send BetaApps traffic to eu-central-1-alt pool which was not touched in the maint window. Also lowered max_concurrent_requests from 12->6 for affected pool to reduce queueing. Pushing a temporary rate-limit for non-critical tenants.

harper (support): BetaApps acknowledged routing change and asked for ETA.

maintenance-bot: snapshot-consolidation job cluster-id sc-7789 paused

diego (sre): After routing change, BetaApps p99 dropped to ~260ms within 2m. Good signal. Need to validate host-level fix before global rollback.

sam (infra): Canary plan: 3 nodes (gpu-node-17/18/21) rollback firmware to v11.1.9, reboot, run stress perf and long-run iostat. Rolling every 15m with health checks.

li (eng-runtime): Also applied a patch to the inference agent to avoid writing large temporary KV swap files to local NVMe during batch eviction; now it spills to tmpfs when below 2GB free as fallback. That should reduce write bursts.

diego (sre): Can we get a quick perf snapshot after canary?

maintenance-bot: firmware-rollback playbook started on canary (play id: fw-rb-441).

li (eng-runtime): Canary results (gpu-node-17) post-rollback:
```
iostat -x 1 3
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s  wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         3.00    22.00    512   20480   6.1    1.8   21.3
```
```
$p95/p99 for local test workload
p95: 120ms -> 140ms
p99: 3.2s -> 220ms
```

diego (sre): Nice. Looks like rollback fixes the stall. Kernel dmesg no longer shows AER or GPU lockups.

sam (infra): Proceeding with phased rollback across the region at 5-node batches. Pausing any consolidation or heavy IO ops until region fully validated.

harper (support): I'll update BetaApps with the rollback plan and ETA ~2 hours, ask them to validate production traffic after we finish.

li (eng-runtime): After rollback we also keep reduced batch sizes and KV spill-to-tmpfs for 24h as safety. We'll ship a hotfix to the agent in the next 48h to make spill behaviour adaptive instead of threshold-based.

diego (sre): Postmortem items we should capture:
- Root cause: GPU firmware v11.2.x + NVMe consolidation heavy writes -> PCIe/AER errors -> GPU kernel hang + NVMe timeouts -> p99 spikes
- Immediate mitigations: route affected customers to alt pool, pause consolidation, firmware rollback, runtime batching changes
- Follow-ups: vendor firmware coordination + NVMe firmware check, CI perf test for firmware-driver combos, agent spill-to-tmpfs improvement, schedule maintenance window review.

alerts-bot: betaapps-p99-alert cleared (alert id: a-6633)

harper (support): BetaApps confirmed latency normalized and they see reduced retries. Thanks team. Posting to customer-facing incident summary.

sam (infra): Opening vendor escalation ticket and CC'ing provider. Also adding a preflight checklist for future firmware pushes (nvme firmware check + small canary writes).

diego (sre): I'll draft the runbook entry: "GPU firmware + NVMe IO saturation -> inference p99" with diagnostic commands (iostat, nvme-cli fw-log, dmesg, nvidia-smi) and automated remediation steps.

li (eng-runtime): Logging this as an infra-regression incident and creating a perf regression test that runs in staging with various firmware/driver matrices.

harper (support): Closing customer escalation once full rollback done and vendor ticket filed.

diego (sre): Keep updates in this thread until fully remediated. Great cross-team response.
